item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 280531
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located about 155 miles southwest of Cabo San Lazaro, Mexico,
on Hurricane Nolo, located a few hundred miles southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical Storm Rachel, located a few
hundred miles southwest of southern Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (EP91):
A broad area of low pressure located well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands continues to become better organized. Environmental
conditions are expected to be conducive for further development, and
a tropical depression is likely to form during the next day or so.
The system should move generally northeastward and remain well east
of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Rachel are issued under
WMO header WTPZ33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Rachel are issued
under WMO header WTPZ23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP3.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Polo Public Advisory Number 30a
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM MST Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 280544
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Intermediate Advisory Number 30A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
1100 PM MST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...LIFE-THREATENING WINDS AND FLASH FLOODS EXPECTED OVER PORTIONS 
OF BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR AND SONORA MONDAY AND TUESDAY...
...CONDITIONS EXPECTED TO BEGIN TO DETERIORATE MONDAY MORNING IN 
BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM MST...0600 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...23.2N 114.0W
ABOUT 260 MI...420 KM W OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 155 MI...250 KM SW OF CABO SAN LAZARO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...954 MB...28.17 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has upgraded the Hurricane Watch to a 
Hurricane Warning along the coast of Mainland Mexico from Bahia 
Kino to Guaymas.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, from Punta Abreojos to Santa Fe
* East coast of Baja California Sur, from Loreto to Santa Rosalia
* Mainland Mexico from Bahia Kino to Huatabampito
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, north of Punta Abreojos to
Punta Eugenia
* East coast of Baja California Sur, south of Loreto to San
Evaristo
* East coast of Baja California Sur, north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Bautista
* Mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, north of Punta Abreojos to
Punta Eugenia.
* East coast of Baja California Sur, south of Loreto to San
Evaristo.
* East coast of Baja California Sur, north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Bautista
* Mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area, in this case within 18 to 36 
hours.  Preparations to protect life and property should be rushed 
to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area, in this case within the next 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, generally within 36
hours.
 
Interests in the remainder of Baja California Sur, and the remainder
of Sonora and northern Sinaloa should monitor the progress of Polo.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM MST (0600 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located
near latitude 23.2 North, longitude 114.0 West. Polo is moving
toward the north near 10 mph (17 km/h). This motion should continue 
for the next several hours followed by a turn toward the northeast 
on Monday. On the forecast track, Polo is expected to approach the 
west coast of Baja California Sur on Monday, move across the 
peninsula Monday evening and then approach northwestern mainland 
Mexico late Monday night into early Tuesday morning.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 120 mph (195 km/h) with higher
gusts. Polo is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Polo is forecast to be at or near major
hurricane strength when it reaches Baja California Sur on Monday,
and it is expected to be a hurricane when it makes landfall in
mainland Mexico late Monday night or early Tuesday morning.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105
miles (165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 954 mb (28.17 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected within the warning area
along the west coast of Baja California Sur by late Monday
afternoon, with tropical storm conditions beginning in the southern
portion of the warning area Monday morning. These conditions are
expected to spread northward and eastward across Baja California Sur
on Monday. Hurricane conditions are expected within the Hurricane
Warning area and possible in the watch area in mainland
northwestern Mexico late Monday night through early Tuesday with
tropical storm conditions expected to begin Monday night.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches with maximum amounts of 12 inches across portions of Baja
California Sur. Rainfall totals of 4 to 6 inches with maximum totals
of 8 inches are expected across portions of Sonora. This rainfall 
may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in 
areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURGE: A storm surge could produce significant coastal flooding in
areas of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue affecting the coast of
southwestern Mexico, west-central Mexico, and Baja California Sur
during the next couple of days. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 30
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 280235
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  30
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 PM MST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
Polo is approaching the Baja California Peninsula as a powerful 
major hurricane. Satellite images suggest that the cyclone is 
maintaining its intensity with a ragged eye feature persisting, 
surrounded by intense deep convection. The cloud pattern is a little 
asymmetric, with the coldest cloud tops currently located over the 
western half of the circulation. The latest satellite intensity 
estimates are largely unchanged, and generally range from 100 to 115 
kt. Based on that data and steady state appearance, the initial wind 
speed is held at 110 kt.

The major hurricane is moving northward at about 10 kt on the 
western side of a mid-level ridge that is situated over northern 
Mexico. Polo is forecast to turn northeastward on Monday as a trough 
amplifies over California, taking the core of the hurricane over the 
Baja California Peninsula Monday afternoon or evening. Polo is then 
expected to briefly pass over the Gulf of California before making a 
second landfall in northwestern mainland Mexico Monday night or 
early Tuesday morning. Little change was made to the previous 
forecast, and this one lies near the best-performing models of the 
year so far, HCCA and GDMI.

No significant change in strength is expected before Polo reaches 
Baja California, and based on the model guidance, it seems likely 
to be at or near major hurricane intensity when it makes 
landfall there. Land interaction with the peninsula and an increase 
in wind shear should cause some weakening, but Polo is still 
expected to be a hurricane when it reaches mainland Mexico. After 
the second landfall, rapid weakening is forecast over the rugged 
terrain of Mexico. The NHC intensity forecast is similar to the 
previous one, and in good agreement with the majority of the 
guidance.
 
Although Polo is expected to dissipate before it reaches the 
southern U.S., distant moisture associated with it and the 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Odalys will be transported into the 
southwestern United States during the next few days, and may 
indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash flood threat in 
the region. See products issued by the Weather Prediction Center for 
more information.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Polo is forecast to make landfall on the west coast of the Baja
California Peninsula as a hurricane late Monday, within the 
Hurricane Warning area. Conditions are expected to begin to 
deteriorate there Monday morning, making further preparations 
difficult. Hurricane and tropical storm conditions are expected to 
spread across Baja California through Monday and into mainland 
Mexico on early Tuesday. A storm surge is likely, especially in 
areas of onshore winds.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact Baja California 
Sur along with southern and central portions of Sonora Monday into 
Tuesday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and 
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain. Moisture from Polo 
will support heavy rainfall and flooding potential across the 
Southwest U.S. into the Southern High Plains late Monday into 
Tuesday.
 
3. Dangerous surf and rip currents are likely along portions of
the northwest coast of Mexico and Baja California for the next
couple of days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  28/0300Z 22.8N 114.0W  110 KT 125 MPH
 12H  28/1200Z 24.1N 113.7W  110 KT 125 MPH
 24H  29/0000Z 25.9N 112.4W  100 KT 115 MPH

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 AM CST (0600 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was 
located near latitude 13.2 North, longitude 100.0 West. Rachel is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h). A faster 
west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days. On 
the forecast track, the center of Rachel is expected to remain well 
offshore of the coast of southern Mexico. However, tropical storm 
conditions are possible along the coast of Mexico within the 
tropical storm watch area by Tuesday.
 
Recent satellite-derived wind data indicates that the maximum 
sustained winds have increased to near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Strengthening is forecast during the next few days, and 
Rachel is forecast to become a hurricane on Tuesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles (220 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1001 mb (29.56 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
WIND:  Tropical storm conditions are possible within the watch
area by Tuesday.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Rachel will begin affecting portions of
southern coast of Mexico during the next couple of days.  These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 280246
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
900 PM CST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
The last few visible satellite images of the day indicate that 
Rachel continues to have a broad center. A recently received 
Oceansat-3 scatterometer pass that partially sampled the system a 
few hours ago indicated winds to at least 35 kt about 120 n mi west 
of the center. Objective satellite intensity estimates range from 
35-40 kt and the Dvorak classification from TAFB is T2.5/35 kt. 
Based on these data, and the broad structure of the tropical 
cyclone, the initial intensity is maintained at 35 kt for this 
advisory.
 
Rachel is moving westward at 280/6 kt. The overall track philosophy
has not changed for this forecast. A deep-layer ridge building over
Mexico is expected to steer the cyclone west-northwestward at a
faster forward speed through mid-week. On Thursday, a weakness in
the ridge, caused by a trough over the southwestern United States,
will cause the cyclone to move more slowly on a similar
northwestward heading. The new track forecast is similar to the
advisory, and blends the Google DeepMind (GDM) and HFIP Corrected
Consensus Aid (HCCA).
 
The tropical storm continues to endure approximately 20 kt of
northeasterly shear, which is clearly evident on satellite imagery.
Given the broad structure and moderate to high wind shear, gradual
intensification is forecast over the next couple of days. The shear
is expected to subside early next week and intensification is likely
to continue thereafter, with Rachel forecast to become a hurricane
on Tuesday. Rachel could then track over the cool wake from
Hurricane Polo, though recent drifter data captured vertical
profiles that show high ocean heat content (OHC) persists in the
region. The intensity forecast is on the higher end of the guidance
envelope, and blends the GDM and HCCA solutions.

The analyzed and forecast tropical storm force wind radii for Rachel 
are larger in this forecast than the previous one. Due to the 
proximity of tropical storm force winds to the coast, the government 
of Mexico has issue a Tropical Storm Watch from Punta San Telmo to 
Playa Perula.

Key Messages:

1. Although the core of Rachel is forecast to remain offshore of 
Mexico, tropical storm force winds are possible along a portion of 
the coast of southwestern Mexico in the Tropical Storm Watch area 
on Tuesday.

2. Large waves could produce life-threatening surf and rip current
